attributes.body_ja:
文（ぶん）の終（お）わりの「だって」は、話（はな）し手（て）が聞（き）いた内容（ないよう）を誰（だれ）かに伝（つた）えるときに使（つか）われます。この「だって」は、必（かなら）ず「ん」や「なん」と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。

「だって」は、助動詞（じょどうし）の「だ」と副助詞（ふくじょし）の「って」の組（く）み合（あ）わせです。「なんだって」の意味（いみ）は、以下（いか）のように分（わ）けて考（かんが）えることができます。

なん - 説明（せつめい）を示（しめ）す。

だ - それが事実（じじつ）であることを示（しめ）す。

って - 「と言（い）って」や「と思（おも）って」を短（みじか）くした形（かたち）。

このような成（な）り立（た）ちから、「なんだって」は「(A) だと言（い）われている」や「思（おも）われている」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）すと解釈（かいしゃく）することもできます。ただし、実際（じっさい）には、「(A) だと聞（き）いた」や「(A) らしい」といった軽（かる）いニュアンスで使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「なんだって」は、かなりくだけた言（い）い方（かた）なので、友達（ともだち）との会話（かいわ）で使（つか）うのがいいでしょう。
attributes.body:
When used at the end of sentences, だって often expresses something that has been heard by the speaker. This particular use of だって will always be paired with ん or なん.

As だって is a grouping of the auxiliary verb だ, and the adverbial particle って, なんだって primarily expresses the following:

なん - Presents an explanation.

だ - Determines something to be true.

って - An abbreviation of と言（い）って 'is said' or と思（おも）って 'is thought'.

In this way, it translates quite similarly to 'it is that (A) was said/thought'. Realistically though, it is used in the same way as 'I heard that (A)', or 'it's thought that (A)'.

Caution

なんだって usually comes across as being quite casual, so is best used in conversations with friends.

んだって and らしい ① both convey information from another source, but with different nuances and levels of formality. らしい ① suggests hearsay with a nuance of certainty, indicating the speaker believes it to be true, e.g. 'Apparently it's (A).'. In contrast, んだって is highly casual and includes an explanatory nuance, similar to 'He/she/they said/say (A), you know.'.

first_relatable.title: んだって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that

attributes.body: Both ときいた and んだって express hearsay, but with different nuances and formality. ときいた means 'I heard (A).' and conveys information directly heard by the speaker, e.g. 高いときいた ('I heard it was expensive.'). In contrast, んだって is casual and adds an explanatory nuance, like 'They say (A).' or 'I heard that (A).', e.g. 高いんだって ('They say it's expensive, you know.').

second_relatable.title: んだって
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that

attributes.body: Both express hearsay, but with different tone and usage. んだって is very casual, often used in everyday conversation, and carries an explanatory tone due to んだ, e.g. 明日休みなんだって ('They said tomorrow's a day off, you know.') そうだ is more neutral and indirect, with no explanatory nuance, e.g. 明日休みだそうだ ('I heard tomorrow's a day off.')

first_relatable.title: んだって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: って (a contracted form of と) is a casual quoting particle used to mark direct or indirect speech, thoughts, feelings, or to introduce a topic. んだって, which combines って with the explanatory ん・の, is used to express 'I heard' or 'He/she/they said.' While って can follow any word, んだって requires な before な-Adjectives or nouns.

first_relatable.title: んだって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that

attributes.body: Both expressions involve だって, but their usage differs. んだって appears at the end of a sentence and means 'I hear (A)' or 'they say (A)', with an explanatory nuance added by ん. In contrast, だって is more flexible. It can appear at the beginning, middle, or end of a sentence, and has several meanings. It can function as a casual 'because', 'even though', or 'they say (A)', depending on context.

first_relatable.title: んだって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that

second_relatable.title: だって
second_relatable.meaning: I heard/was said, Because, But, Even or also, Even if or even though

attributes.body: These two expressions are similar in that both can serve as casual expressions of hearsay, i.e. 'they say (A)' or 'I hear (A)'. The difference is that んだって has a slightly more explanatory and emphatic nuance due to the presence of ん, while とか has an uncertain or non-specific tone, i.e. 'I hear (A) or something', because of the presence of the question particle か.

first_relatable.title: んだって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that

second_relatable.title: とか
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that… something like, They said ... or something
